title: Unified Retention DSL and Live Audit Playbook for Prompt/Response Telemetry
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers need a single, auditable way to declare retention for different kinds of telemetry (prompts, responses, request logs, metrics) that respects tenant residency, supports conditional sampling, and produces tamper-evident evidence bundles on demand. Current UI offers per-route TTLs and several exporters but lacks a portable policy language and a documented audit playbook for legal/infosec reviews.

Goal: Design a compact Retention DSL (declarative policy language) and a Live Audit Playbook that operators can use to: (1) express residency-aware retention rules by route, model, or tenant; (2) specify differential sampling and hold rules; (3) trigger certified evidence exports via API or console; (4) surface compliance proofs (hash manifests, signatures) in the Console and automated reports. Deliverables: DSL spec, API contract for evidence export, console UX wireframes, backend enforcement plan, compliance test suite, and rollout checklist.
acceptance_criteria: DSL spec document published in Confluence with grammar, examples, and residency operators
API contract (REST + sample SDK call) for on-demand evidence export that returns signed archival bundles
Console wireframes for policy editor and live audit runbook approved by Design and Legal
End-to-end integration test demonstrating TTL enforcement, sampling, and an evidence bundle creation for a test tenant in eu-west-1
Security review completed and KMS/HSM flows validated for evidence signing
Migration plan for existing per-route TTLs with opt-in conversion tool
implementation_notes: Design DSL with first-class operators: keep, delete, sample(rate), legal_hold, residency(region_list), max_age(days)
Back-end evaluator implemented as stateless rule engine that compiles DSL to enforcement jobs; integrate with existing retention worker and archival pipeline
Evidence export API should accept a snapshot window and policy version and return S3-presigned archive + manifest.json + signature header
For residency, tie policy evaluation to route->tenant->region resolution; include fallback behavior for multi-region tenants
Console: inline policy linter, preview estimated storage impact, and a 'Run audit' wizard that records operator actions
Provide migration CLI that reads current per-route mapping and suggests equivalent DSL statements with diff preview
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (spec): finalize DSL and API contract; security review; 2-week design reviews
Phase 1 (backend): implement rule compiler and retention worker hooks in a feature branch; unit + integration tests
Phase 2 (console + API): provide policy editor, linter, and evidence-export endpoint behind feature flag; internal dogfood with 3 teams
Phase 3 (beta): invite 5 enterprise customers to test migrations and evidence exports; collect compliance feedback
Phase 4 (GA): enable opt-in conversion tool and enable policy editor for all tenants; publish audit playbook and runbook
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: retention_enforcement_failures (count) - alert if > 1/hour for any tenant
Log: policy_compiler_errors with sample of failing DSL inputs
Audit trail: record operator runbook executions and export manifest signatures for 5 years in immutable store
SLO: evidence_export_success >= 99.5% for enterprise tenants during beta
